 WTA Tokyo Day 2 Predictions Including Naomi Osaka vs Jasmine Paolini 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 Day two at the WTA Tokyo Open will see a full slate of first-round matches contested and, as always, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, including Sorana Cirstea vs Maya Joint . But who will advance to the next round in the Japanese capital? 
 WTA Tokyo Day 2 Predictions
 Tereza Valentova vs Mia Pohankova
 Head-to-head : first meeting
 19-year-old Tereza Valentova defeated Zhang Shuai for the second time in the last seven days to qualify for the main draw and will make her debut against Mia Pohankova. Valentova has already shown she belongs at this level and will look to make some inroads this week to cap off a breakthrough season. Pohankova has a career-high ranking of #144 and did play well in Wuhan, but Valentova is someway ahead of her in terms of experience and ability at this stage of their careers. She should win this.
 Prediction: Valentova in 3 
 Maria Sakkari vs Yulia Putintseva
 Head-to-head : Sakkari 3-1 Putintseva
 Former world #3 Maria Sakkari reached the quarterfinals in Wuhan and is playing some solid tennis in a phase of the season she has historically enjoyed. She is currently ranked #30 and has no points to defend this week, so will be looking to secure her spot in the top 30. The Greek player has won the last three matches against Yulia Putintseva and will look to extend that streak.
 Putintseva earned her main draw spot by winning two qualifying matches to reach the WTA Tokyo main draw. The Kazakh is a gritty player and will fight for every point, and also possesses useful variety that can make opponents uncomfortably. However, Sakkari’s current form and confidence make her the favourite. She might have to go the distance, but should have enough to advance.
 Prediction: Sakkari in 3 
 Jan 20, 2023; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; Maria Sakkari of Greece hits a shot against Zhu Lin of China on day five of the 2023 Australian Open tennis tournament at Melbourne Park. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-USA TODAY Sports 
 Diane Parry vs Cristina Bucsa
 Head-to-head : Parry 1-0 Bucsa
 Diane Parry has had her best season yet in 2026, but she has lost six straight matches since winning her maiden WTA title in Monterrey. The losses haven’t been close either, as she hasn’t won a single set. Cristina Bucsa is on a five-match losing streak, but she’s played here before, and given Parry has so badly lost her way in recent weeks, this looks a great opportunity for Bucsa to get a much-neeeded win at WTA Tokyo.
 Prediction: Bucsa in 3 
 Naomi Osaka vs Jasmine Paolini
 Head-to-head : Paolini 1-0 Osaka
 Four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has posted a strong 2026 season and will make her first appearance at at WTA Tokyo since 2022. She has been to the finals twice here but will look to go one step further this time and win her first title since 2021. Jasmine Paolini is a nightmare opponent when at her best, but she has struggled for consistency this season. Osaka’s superior form and home-court advantage make her the favourite.
 Prediction: Osaka in 2
